questions.question: What does the `pop` method of `LinkedStack` return?

options.A: The node object at the top of the stack
options.B: The element stored in the top node
options.C: The index of the top element

questions.explanation:
The `pop` method retrieves `self.head.element` and returns it as the stack’s top element. (Source Page: [8])  

---

questions.question: Under which condition does the `pop` method raise an `Empty` exception?

options.D: When the stack contains exactly one element

questions.explanation:
The code checks `if self.is_empty(): raise Empty(...)`, so an exception is raised if the stack is empty. (Source Page: [8])

questions.explanation:

questions.question: Why are `__slots__` used in the `Node` class definition?

options.A: To enforce type checking on attributes
options.B: To reduce memory usage when many nodes are created
options.C: To allow dynamic addition of new attributes

questions.explanation:

questions.question: In Python’s array‑based list, what is the time complexity of `insert` or `pop` at index k?
questions.explanation:
The context notes that inserting or popping at index k costs O(n − k + 1) time due to element shifting. (Source Page: [38])

questions.question: How many variables does each `LinkedStack` instance maintain?
questions.explanation:
The implementation keeps two variables: a reference to the head node and (implicitly) the size. (Source Page: [6])

questions.question: Which line of code updates the head pointer after a `pop` operation?
questions.explanation:
The line `self.head = self.head.next` bypasses the former top node. (Source Page: [8])
